blocking the PI3K pathway inhibits neuropegulin‐1 mediated rescue of neurotoxity induced by A β 1–42.

NRG1 protects neuronal cells from the neurotoxic effects of Aβ1-42 and that this neuroprotection is mediated via the phosphatidyinositol 3‐ kinase (PI3K) and the mitogen‐activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the PI3K/Akt pathway in the neuroprotective effect of neuregulin-1.
the role of phosphatidylinositide 3‐kinases (PI3Ks) and mitogen‐activated protein kinase (MAPK) in the neuroprotective effects of NRG1.
the role of NRG1 and its downstream signalling pathways in the neuroprotection against Aβ1–2 induced neurotoxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NRG1 prevents Aβ1–2‐induced neurodegeneration by activating the PI3K‐Akt pathway and that this pathway plays a crucial role in NRG1‐mediated neuroprotection.
NRG1 signalling through the PI3K pathway is involved in the protection of neuronal cells from the toxicity induced by Aβ.

NRG1‐mediated neuroprotection is mediated by the phosphatidyliol 3‐kinse pathway.

the PI3K‐Akt pathway is essential for the NRG1‐mediated protection against Aβ‐induced neurodegeneration.
